svg.aria-label: Two warnings behind Barbalat's lemma. Left: f(t) = e^(−t) sin(e^(2t)) tends to zero, but its derivative oscillates ever faster and does not tend to zero. Right: f(t) = sin(ln t) has a derivative that tends to zero, but f itself keeps oscillating between −1 and 1 and has no limit
svg.title: Two warnings behind Barbalat's lemma. Left: f(t) = e^(−t) sin(e^(2t)) tends to zero, but its derivative oscillates ever faster and does not tend to zero. Right: f(t) = sin(ln t) has a derivative that tends to zero, but f itself keeps oscillating between −1 and 1 and has no limit

g.text: ḟ = cos(ln t)/t → 0, but f has no limit
Barbalat: if f has a finite limit and ḟ is uniformly continuous (for example, f̈ bounded), then ḟ → 0.
